reviewer: early_windows_review; non-author of Win32 HeldFile repair and its r2 hash extent delta. Earlier unchanged PE parser authored by this reviewer is outside this incremental approval.
scope: Only r1→r2 two-line hash extent repair and associated new synthetic control; preserves r1 independent review and finding.
decision: No blocking finding in this selected delta; prior P2 hash-span mismatch is closed for the reviewed implementation. Actual Windows resource verification is still required.
reasoning: Both initial and final hashing now traverse exactly self.size, which was already selected from bounded original-handle FileStandardInfo on Windows; every byte admitted to reads is covered by SHA.

The native size is checked against the input limit before hashing; chunks remain at most 1 MiB, each read retains its extent/work-budget/short-read checks, and finishing retains before/after same-API native identity and metadata checks.

POSIX keeps identical selected length because self.size is initialized from self.initial.st_size. Native ABI, CreateFileW flags, CRT ownership transfer, non-reparse checks, original-handle closure, PE parsing and resource acceptance were untouched.

Independent current-source control hashes all six bytes despite Python diagnostic sizes 0/3/10; a suffix-only change with unchanged mocked metadata is rejected by final hash and original fd is closed. This proves the extent invariant only, not an actual Windows concurrent-write scenario.
limitations: No Cargo, CI, Windows API execution, formal app, actual PE inspection or old artifact result reader was run for this review.
The supplied 13-case author log is reviewed evidence, not claimed as an independently rerun 13-case suite.
No result of the pending actual Windows resource/manifest checks is inferred; source review and owned-file model controls do not establish those outcomes.
